claim_hierarchy.claim: Near-complete Ross aggregate recovery was produced by strongly unequal local restoration; abundance returned largely where it had been lost, while endpoint spatial composition remained altered at both six-component and three-colony grains.
claim_hierarchy.boundary: State-restoration magnitude is spatial-grain dependent. The robust claim is incomplete restoration at both biologically natural grains, not a universal 2.4% recovery score.

claim_hierarchy.claim: At six-component grain, all three complete Ross down-up episodes had high inverse-path fidelity while state restoration was weak or negative.
claim_hierarchy.boundary: Episodes are descriptive within-series calibration, not independent replicates.

claim_hierarchy.claim: Persistent decline at Palmer and Signy reweighted breeding structure beyond proportional thinning.
claim_hierarchy.boundary: Specific vital-rate mechanisms are not identified.

claim_hierarchy.claim: Beaufort growth after capacity release reweighted breeding structure beyond proportional expansion while independent inter-island export declined.
claim_hierarchy.boundary: Census and movement evidence are independent streams, not mediation.

claim_hierarchy.claim: Unequal local recovery can yield near-complete aggregate recovery and high path reversal while leaving spatial state incompletely restored; apparent state restoration depends on observation grain.
claim_hierarchy.boundary: No universal scale-free restoration index or causal law is claimed.

main_sentence: Near-complete aggregate recovery was produced by differential local recovery: the population recovered where it had declined, but not in the same proportions, and spatial structure remained altered at both natural grains.
withdrawn_claims: Ross restored or re-expressed the pre-shock spatial state
high inverse-path fidelity implies complete state restoration
state restoration equals 2.4% as a scale-invariant property
near-complete aggregate recovery means most breeding components nearly recovered
the focal result demonstrates latent spatial memory
